steps: Confirm proximal DVT with compression venous ultrasonography (D-dimer to help exclude when pretest probability is low).
Anticoagulate once confirmed: DOAC monotherapy (rivaroxaban or apixaban) first-line, or parenteral heparin/LMWH bridged to warfarin (target INR 2-3); warfarin not DOACs for antiphospholipid syndrome.

Treat at least 3 months; for first VTE consider extended/indefinite anticoagulation when there is no identifiable risk factor or a persistent risk factor (Harrison de-emphasises 'provoked vs unprovoked').
For cancer-associated VTE use LMWH or a DOAC (apixaban/edoxaban; avoid DOAC with GI cancer) and continue until cancer-free.
Compression stockings for symptomatic relief; check renal function for dosing; counsel on PE warning signs.

drugRefs.dose: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily
drugRefs.why: First-line single-drug oral anticoagulation; no parenteral lead-in required.

drugRefs.dose: 15 mg twice daily for 21 days, then 20 mg once daily
drugRefs.why: Alternative first-line single-drug DOAC; no parenteral lead-in required.

drugRefs.dose: 1.5 mg/kg once daily (or 1 mg/kg twice daily)
drugRefs.why: Parenteral option for cancer-associated VTE, pregnancy, or bridging to warfarin; dose per renal function.
Option for cancer-associated VTE; avoid in luminal GI cancers due to bleeding risk.

drugRefs.dose: titrated to INR 2–3 (with parenteral heparin/LMWH cover until therapeutic)
drugRefs.why: Preferred over DOACs in antiphospholipid syndrome; requires overlapping LMWH until INR therapeutic.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Deep Vein Thrombosis & Venous Thromboembolism (pp. 2204–2207)
ASH 2020 Guidelines for Management of Venous Thromboembolism
NICE NG158 — Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing

confirm: Unilateral leg pain/swelling/tenderness; risk-stratify (Wells), D-dimer if low probability, compression US confirms.
